WMBY.name: Delivery Regular
condition_labels: Delivery accounts for ≥ 50% of dining spend
Delivery appears in at least 3 weeks
Delivery order count significantly higher than groceries (≥ 1.5x)
WMBY.core_categories: Meals, fast food, breakfast, late-night snacks, and other delivery-based dining purchases made through delivery platforms or food delivery apps.
guardrails: Do not assume high-frequency online shopping indicates 'shopping addiction' or lack of self-control.
Do not describe frequent online shopping as 'wasteful' or 'reckless spending'.
Do not assume purchased items are unnecessary or have no practical use.
Do not infer user income, wealth, or financial status from purchase amounts.
Do not infer user gender, occupation, or social status from purchased items.
Do not label high-frequency small orders as 'impulsive shopping' unless supported by other clear behavioral data.
It's okay to playfully reference typical online shopping scenarios like cart, bundling, coupons, and delivery notifications, but keep it light, relatable, and non-shaming.
distinguish: When purchasing milk tea via delivery platforms, if the specific merchant can be identified as a tea brand, prioritize counting it under milk tea consumption traits.
WMBY.focus: High frequency + consistency + delivery-based dining + clear delivery usage habits

NCXM.name: Milk Tea Lifeline
condition_labels: Tea drinks appear in at least 3 weeks
Repeat purchase at same tea shop ≥ 3 times
Tea drink orders significantly higher than snacks/desserts (≥ 1.5x)
NCXM.core_categories: Consumption of freshly made tea drinks: milk tea, new-style tea, fruit tea, fresh milk tea, etc.
guardrails: Do not judge users as 'addicted' based on milk tea purchase frequency
Do not infer users' weight, health status, or dietary issues from tea drink bills
Do not comment that users drink 'too much' milk tea or 'should drink less'
Do not describe frequent small-amount tea purchases as wasteful
Do not assume users buy milk tea due to stress, fatigue, or emotional issues
Do not infer users' income or economic level from the brands they buy
May use lighthearted internet expressions like 'life-saving', 'happiness buff', 'refill'
Personality interpretation should highlight small self-indulgence, daily rituals, and frequent tea-drinking habits
distinguish: Milk Tea Lifeline ≠ Takeout Monthly Subscriber: if users buy milk tea via delivery platforms, prioritize milk tea traits. Follow 'specific consumption category > consumption channel' — do not over-score 'Takeout Monthly Subscriber' just because users order milk tea delivery.
NCXM.focus: Purchase frequency > Consistency > Repeat purchases > Spending amount

TDLD.name: Restaurant Radar
TDLD.core_categories: Dine-in restaurants, specialty dining, cafés, brunch spots, dessert shops, bistro bars — any food & drink experience with a vibe.
guardrails: Don't label frequent new restaurant visits as 'trend-following'
Don't assume users dine out just for photos, social media, or hype spots
Don't judge users as 'wasting money' or 'can't manage life' based on higher dine-in spending
Don't infer income, wealth, or social status from restaurant tier or spending amount
Don't infer weight, health, or eating habits from dining frequency
Don't assume a high new-store rate means users are fickle
Light expressions like 'hit or miss', 'hidden gem', 'unlock a new spot' are fine
Focus interpretation on curiosity, novelty-seeking, merchant diversity, and experience orientation
distinguish: Restaurant Radar ≠ Delivery Devotee — Delivery Devotee is about convenience, frequency, and ordering in; Restaurant Radar is about dine-in, variety, and exploration.
Restaurant Radar ≠ Boba Lifeline — if consumption involves multiple brands of milk tea, fruit tea, or other made-to-order drinks, prioritize Boba Lifeline identification.

If a user frequently visits the same chain coffee shop, don't label them as a spot-hunter just because of high frequency; if they consistently visit different independent cafés, brunch spots, etc., that strengthens the Restaurant Radar score.
TDLD.focus: Merchant diversity + new-store rate + sustained exploration behavior

KDZH.name: Parcel Summoner
condition_labels: Online shopping in at least 3 weeks
KDZH.core_categories: Online purchases of physical goods from general e-commerce, brand online stores, social commerce, etc., such as clothing, home goods, digital accessories, daily necessities, stationery, small items.
guardrails: Don't assume high-frequency shopping equals addiction or lack of self-control
Don't describe frequent online shopping as 'wasteful' or 'overspending'
Don't assume purchased items are unnecessary or useless
Don't infer income, wealth, or financial status from spending amounts
Don't infer gender, occupation, or social identity from purchased items
Don't label small frequent orders as 'impulsive spending' without clear behavioral data
It's okay to joke about carts, bundling, coupons, delivery notifications, etc., but keep it light, relatable, and shame-free
KDZH.focus: Shopping frequency and consistency > total spending amount

CCLJ.name: Market Money Manager
condition_labels: Groceries account for ≥ 30% of food & drink spending
Grocery trips clearly outnumber takeout orders (≥ 1.5x)
CCLJ.core_categories: Wet markets / fresh supermarkets / community grocery stores / fruit shops / meat, poultry, eggs & dairy / grains, oils & condiments / online fresh food platforms — any household grocery spending.
guardrails: Don't describe price-checking, discounts, or value-seeking as 'stingy' or 'cheap'
Don't infer low income, financial hardship, or limited spending power from grocery buying behavior
Don't infer gender, marital status, or family role from grocery shopping frequency
Don't assume frequent grocery buyers cook every day themselves
Don't describe buying discounted or promotional items as 'being greedy for a bargain'
Don't judge a lifestyle as 'healthier' or 'more disciplined' just because takeout spending is low
Feel free to playfully reference scenes like grocery shopping, price-checking, picking produce, or stocking up — but highlight planning skills, life savvy, and a sense of control over spending
distinguish: Market Money Manager ≠ Takeout Monthly Pass Holder
Frequent grocery buying, low takeout frequency → stronger 'Market Money Manager' traits. Frequent takeout, little grocery buying → stronger 'Takeout Monthly Pass Holder' traits.
The two aren't mutually exclusive. If a user orders takeout often on weekdays but regularly buys groceries on weekends, calculate Money Personality match separately.
Market Money Manager ≠ Delivery Summoner
Even if groceries (vegetables, fruit, meat, rice, oil, etc.) are bought through online platforms, they should still be identified as grocery spending, not general online shopping.
CCLJ.focus: Purchase frequency + consistency > single transaction amount

JZZY.name: Refined Living Curator
JZZY.core_categories: Skincare / Makeup / Perfume & Fragrance / Apparel & Fashion / Accessories / Hair / Nails / Beauty treatments / Premium lifestyle items / Designer home goods — any spending that clearly boosts personal image, aesthetic, or quality of life.
guardrails: Don't describe quality or image spending as 'vain', 'gold-digging', or 'competitive'
Don't infer income, family background, or social class from brand, price, or spending amount
Don't assume users buy beauty, fashion, or fragrance for others' approval
Don't infer gender from beauty, hair, or nail spending
Don't equate 'refined' with expensive, luxury, or designer brands
Don't label users as consumerist or overspenders just because they spend more on quality
Use positive terms like 'ritual', 'texture', 'self-care', 'discerning'
Interpretation should highlight aesthetic choices, quality awareness, attention to detail, and life experience
distinguish: Refined Living Curator ≠ Delivery Summoner
'Delivery Summoner' focuses on high-frequency online physical goods purchases;
'Refined Living Curator' focuses on the type of goods/services bought and a quality lifestyle tendency.

20 online purchases in a month including daily essentials, stationery, digital accessories → stronger Delivery Summoner trait. Consistent purchases of skincare, fragrance, fashion, plus hair/nail spending → stronger Refined Living Curator trait.
If a user buys skincare online, both 'online shopping' and 'quality spending' traits can coexist; final score determines the dominant persona.
Refined Living Curator ≠ Grocery Investor

Even if a user frequently buys imported ingredients, organic produce, or premium supermarket items, as long as the spending is essentially on household groceries, it should be prioritized under 'Grocery Investor'.
JZZY.focus: Category diversity + consistency + quality lifestyle spending share > single item price
JZZY.interpretation: You're willing to pay for 'texture' in life. Skincare, makeup, fashion, perfume, or those little things that make everyday life more refined and comfortable — they might all show up on your bill. You don't necessarily go for the priciest, but you care about quality, design, and experience. For you, being refined isn't about filling life with expensive stuff — it's about thoughtfully choosing the lifestyle you love within your means. You can save where it counts, but you never settle when it matters.

DYSJ.name: Subscription Collector
condition_labels: Regular charges from the same merchant (requires billing history)
≥ 3 consecutive charges for 3 billing cycles (requires billing history)
Subscriptions account for ≥ 40% of digital service spending
DYSJ.core_categories: Streaming memberships / music subscriptions / cloud storage / software subscriptions / AI tools / reading memberships / learning platforms / fitness or lifestyle service memberships—any subscription-based spending with recurring payment characteristics.
guardrails: Do not assume users forgot to cancel or are unaware of being charged
Do not describe multiple memberships as 'wasting money,' 'getting ripped off,' or 'paying the stupid tax'
Do not assume users don't actually use these subscriptions
Do not infer income or financial status based on number or price of subscriptions
Do not judge subscription value as simply 'worth it' or 'not worth it'
Do not infer lack of financial management skills just because of many auto-renewals
It's okay to poke fun at typical scenarios like Premium, auto-renewal, or membership count, but avoid spending shame
Personality interpretation should highlight digital lifestyle, convenience, service experience, and ongoing subscription habits
distinguish: Subscription Collector ≠ Whale Spender
Game memberships, Battle Passes, monthly cards, etc., may have both subscription and gaming spending attributes.

If the bill clearly identifies gaming-related payments, prioritize enhancing the 'Whale Spender' trait; regular subscriptions like streaming, software, or cloud services fall under 'Subscription Collector'.
DYSJ.focus: Active subscription count + recurrence + continuity > total subscription amount

KJZS.name: Top-Up Warrior
condition_labels: Game spending appears in at least 3 weeks
Gaming accounts for ≥ 30% of entertainment spending
≥ 3 transactions on the same game / platform
≥ 3 purchases of virtual content (e.g., points, skins, battle passes)
KJZS.core_categories: Mobile game top-ups / PC game in-app purchases / Console game digital spending / Game points / Virtual currency / Skins / Characters / Equipment / Battle Pass / Season Pass / Game subscription cards — any game-related virtual spending.
guardrails: Do not judge users as having gaming addiction, internet addiction, or obsession based on spending frequency
Do not describe game top-ups as 'wasteful', 'throwing money away', or 'paying a stupidity tax'
Do not assume virtual goods are 'not worth paying for' just because they have no physical form
Do not infer users' income, wealth, or financial status from top-up amounts
Do not infer users' gender, age, or occupation from game genre, characters, or platform
Do not assume users top up to show off, compete, or gain an advantage
Do not directly label frequent game spending as impulse spending or lack of self-control
Use common gaming community terms like 'top-up', 'skin', 'gacha', 'battle pass', 'recharge'
Focus interpretation on gaming interest, virtual content spending, and paying for entertainment experiences
distinguish: Top-Up Warrior ≠ Subscription Collector
Game subscription cards, Battle Pass, game memberships may be periodic, but if clearly identifiable as game-related services, prioritize strengthening the 'Top-Up Warrior' trait.
Top-Up Warrior ≠ Express Summoner
Buying game-related physical items online (e.g., controllers, keyboards, consoles, physical game cartridges) is essentially physical shopping and should not be directly treated as 'top-up'.
KJZS.focus: In-game spending frequency + consistency + entertainment spending share > single top-up amount

DQOL.name: Earth Online Player
condition_labels: ≥ 2 independent travel cycles (90 days per cycle, requires historical billing)
Travel accounts for ≥ 15% of non-fixed spending
Spending chain includes ≥ 2 categories: long-distance transport + accommodation / tickets
DQOL.core_categories: Flights / High-speed rail & long-distance trains / Long-distance buses / Hotels & homestays / Travel platforms / Scenic spot tickets / Museum & exhibition tickets / Local travel transport / Cross-border transport / Travel-related activities & experiences — non-daily travel spending
guardrails: Do not infer user income, wealth, or family economic status based on travel frequency
Do not describe travel spending as 'waste money', 'can't save', or 'not doing serious work'
Do not judge users as 'rich', 'extravagant', or 'showing off' based on flight or hotel prices
Do not assume high travel frequency means the user is avoiding work, study, or real life
Do not infer user occupation, nationality, family background, or long-term residence based on travel destinations
Do not assume travel spending is always leisure travel; it may include visiting family, studying, business, etc.
If billing cannot distinguish travel purpose, use neutral terms like 'trip', 'exploration', 'experience'
Use elements like 'map, coordinates, suitcase, boarding pass, next stop' to create light humor
Personality interpretation should highlight cross-region travel, experience-based spending, and continuous exploration in billing patterns
distinguish: Earth Online Player ≠ Commuter Machine

The key difference is daily repetitive travel vs. non-daily travel. Ordinary city transport should not increase 'Earth Online Player' score just because of high frequency; it requires travel signals like cross-city spending, long-distance transport, and accommodation.
Earth Online Player ≠ Restaurant Radar
Going to different restaurants during a trip does not mean all those expenses count toward 'Earth Online Player'.
Daily continuous exploration of different restaurants → Restaurant Radar; Hotels / flights / attractions / travel experiences → Earth Online Player
If a user enjoys both travel and restaurant exploration, both money personalities can score high simultaneously.
DQOL.focus: Travel cycles + multi-category spending chain + cross-region features > single trip amount

TQYD.name: Perpetual Commuter
TQYD.core_categories: Subway / MRT / Bus / Public transport card / Taxi / Ride-hailing / Bike-sharing / City ferry — daily urban transport spending
guardrails: Don't assume user is an office worker or student based on transport spending
Don't infer user has no car, can't afford one, or has limited finances from public transport use
Don't judge user as 'lazy', 'extravagant', or 'wasteful' based on ride-hailing frequency
Don't assume frequent movement means long commutes or high life stress
Don't infer user's specific job, school, or schedule from travel times
Don't infer or generate sensitive location info like home or workplace from transport routes
Don't rank one transport mode as 'better' or 'more economical' than another
Use light expressions like 'on the go / tap in / transfer / next stop / moving / route'
Focus interpretation on frequent, consistent, routine urban movement spending
distinguish: Perpetual Commuter ≠ EarthOnline Player
Daily intra-city repeat movement → commute; non-daily cross-region movement → travel
If Grab, Uber, or subway appear during travel, combine with location + hotel/flight spending to reduce their weight for 'Perpetual Commuter'
TQYD.focus: Frequency × Consistency × Daily routine > Total transport spending

MHZT.name: Furry Kid ATM
condition_labels: Pet spending appears in at least 3 weeks
Repeat purchase from same pet merchant ≥ 2 times
MHZT.core_categories: Pet food / Cat & dog food / Pet treats / Cat litter / Pet daily supplies / Toys / Pet grooming / Bathing / Pet hospital / Vet / Pet insurance / Pet boarding / Pet services, and other pet-related spending
guardrails: Do not judge users as 'overindulgent', 'wasteful', or 'irrational' based on pet spending amount
Do not describe pet medical expenses as 'money-burning', 'wasteful', or 'not worth it'
Do not assign this persona based on a single high pet medical expense
Do not assume users cut back on basic needs for their pets
Do not generate value judgments like 'pets more important than people' or 'treating pets better than yourself'
Do not guess the specific pet type (cat, dog, rabbit, etc.) from bills; use 'pet / furry kid' when info is insufficient
Do not infer user's marital status, family structure, living alone, or occupation from pet spending
Do not infer user's income or financial ability from spending amount
May use light expressions like 'furry kid / boss / kibble / treats / toys / picking up the tab / balance'
Persona interpretation should highlight stable pet spending, daily care, and the warmth of being willing to invest in the furry kid
distinguish: Furry Kid ATM ≠ Delivery Summoner
Even if pet supplies are bought via e-commerce, as long as the specific product category is identifiable, prioritize classifying as pet spending.
Buying cat food on Taobao → Furry Kid ATM; buying clothes on e-commerce → Delivery Summoner
Continue following the rule: 'specific spending category > spending channel'
MHZT.focus: Consistency + spending frequency + multi-scenario coverage > single transaction amount

JW.name: Page Chewer
JW.core_categories: Education & training / Books & materials / Stationery & learning supplies / Online courses / Exam registration / Learning software & tools / Paying for knowledge / Morning study-related spending

HAO.name: Black Card Roller
condition_labels: Top category ∈ Online shopping / Beauty & fashion / Dining in
HAO.core_categories: High-ticket dining / Beauty & fashion / Luxury goods / Electronics / Entertainment experiences / Travel and other consistently high-ticket spending

SCTZ.name: Small-Bill Sprinkler
condition_labels: And daily ≥ 2.5 transactions (calibrated: to distinguish from Penny Pincher)
SCTZ.core_categories: Convenience stores / Coffee & milk tea / Snacks & street food / Public transit / Ride-hailing / Daily essentials / Small online purchases / High-frequency scan-to-pay — scattered small spending

SQDS.name: Savings Master
condition_labels: Daily spending ≤ ¥50 for ≥ 3 consecutive days (exclude fixed expenses, ≥ 2 transactions/day)
Weeks with weekly spending ≤ ¥350 for ≥ 2 weeks (exclude fixed expenses, ≥ 4 spending days/week)
SQDS.core_categories: Basic meals / Public transit / Daily essentials / Basic clothing / Rent and other necessary living expenses; also spotlight bill patterns with low ticket sizes and low non-essential big spending.

YXDW.name: Night Owl
condition_labels: ≥ 3 transactions on a single late night
YXDW.core_categories: Takeout / late-night snacks / ride-hailing / online shopping / convenience stores / entertainment and other late-night spending from 21:00–05:00
do_not_say: Staying up late is bad for you

YDDJ.name: End-of-Month Survivor
YDDJ.tone: Finding joy in hardship, month-end survival prose, self-mocking banter
YDDJ.core_categories: No specific spending category restrictions; mainly identifies a clear 'front-heavy, back-light' spending rhythm within the same billing cycle.

SJNS.name: Social Connector
SJNS.core_categories: Friend transfers / AA payments / Red packets / Paying for others / Group dinner settlements / Gifts / Activity fee splits and other social money flows

YDSS.name: One-Store Loyalist
condition_labels: Single merchant accounts for ≥ 50% of transactions
≥ 4 transactions at the same merchant in one day (excluding transport and platforms)
≥ 2 transactions daily at the same merchant for ≥ 3 consecutive days (excluding transport and platforms)
≥ 30 transactions at the same merchant in a month (excluding food delivery / e-commerce platforms)
YDSS.core_categories: High-frequency repeat spending at the same coffee shop / milk tea shop / restaurant / convenience store / supermarket / brand store / e-commerce shop, etc.; excludes misidentification caused by unified merchant names on food delivery platforms

DSDS.name: Balance Master
DSDS.core_categories: Steady spending across dining, shopping, transport, entertainment, fresh groceries, drinks, daily essentials, learning, and more — with no single category dominating.

SJWF.name: Data Escapee
SJWF.core_categories: Insufficient valid transactions / Incomplete spending category coverage / Too short a statistical period / Lack of data to identify spending habits

YRBZ.name: One-Day Spree
YRBZ.line: Frugal every day, until that one day.

HYM.name: Coupon Connoisseur
HYM.line: Orders without a discount don't deserve to be paid.
